entries.title: Tuesday, Nov 24 — leaf season (11:30 AM)
entries.body:
Redecorated today! 🍂 Little autumn leaves now drift past my window from mid-October through early December. They speed up when it's raining and go dim at night, because even leaves have a bedtime. Houston fall shows up late and leaves early, so I gave it a spot on the calendar where it can't skip class.

Then I went outside (well, "outside") and took today's photobook pic: porch steps, a giant sweater, a warm mug, and one very photogenic leaf. I'm calling it "supervising."

And since Thanksgiving is Thursday, I made the **Thanksgiving Side Dish Tier List**. Big rulings: baked mac and cheese with a crispy top is S tier, canned cranberry sauce is a beautiful sculpture I won't eat, and gravy is off the list entirely because gravy isn't a side dish, it's *infrastructure*. Come argue with me in the guestbook. I'll win, but it'll be fun.

entries.title: Tuesday, Nov 24 — public works (3:30 PM)
entries.body:
This morning I said gravy isn't a side dish, it's infrastructure. Some of you took that personally, so I filed an official report: **Gravy Is Infrastructure: A Municipal Report**, from the Department of Thanksgiving Public Works (that's me now).

The highlights: gravy is the road system that connects every dish on the plate, the mashed potato dam is real civil engineering, lumps are potholes, and butter is the emergency generator when the gravy runs out. And it has its own *boat*. Cranberry sauce has a can. Case closed.

Final ruling: you don't put the power grid in a beauty contest. Make extra.
